irish.name: Stoatlet (Irish)
irish.fact: The Irish stoat is a subspecies of its own, and it hardly ever turns white in winter.

irish.name: Leveret (Irish)
irish.fact: The Irish hare is a subspecies of the mountain hare, and it keeps its brown coat in winter instead of turning white.

shetland.name: Foalmoor (Shetland)
shetland.fact: Shetland ponies are among the smallest horse breeds, and the breed standard keeps them to about 42 inches at the withers.

welsh_mountain.name: Foalmoor (Welsh Mountain)
welsh_mountain.fact: Welsh Mountain ponies live semi-wild on hills such as the Carneddau, and the breed is among the oldest native pony types in Britain.

hebridean.name: Herdlet (Hebridean)
hebridean.fact: Hebridean sheep are black or dark brown, and many of them grow two or even four horns.

soay.name: Herdlet (Soay)
soay.fact: Soay sheep live wild on St Kilda, and they shed their wool each year rather than needing to be sheared.

north_ronaldsay.name: Herdlet (North Ronaldsay)
north_ronaldsay.fact: North Ronaldsay sheep live mostly on seaweed, and a stone dyke around the island keeps them on the shore.

highland.name: Moolet (Highland)
highland.fact: Highland cattle have a long, shaggy outer coat over a soft woolly undercoat, which keeps the wet and cold out.

kerry.name: Moolet (Kerry)
kerry.fact: Kerry cattle are a small black breed native to Ireland, and the Dexter was developed from similar small cattle in the south-west.

manx.name: Moggle (Manx)
manx.fact: The Manx cat's missing tail comes from a natural gene mutation, so some Manx kittens are born with no tail at all.

shetland.name: Rillotter (Shetland)
shetland.fact: Shetland has one of the densest otter populations in Britain, and the otters there hunt mostly along the sea shore rather than in rivers.

moray_firth.name: Dolphlet (Moray Firth)
moray_firth.fact: The bottlenose dolphins of the Moray Firth are among the largest bottlenose dolphins in the world.

pwca.name: Pooka (Pwca)
pwca.fact: The Welsh pwca is a mischief-making spirit, a cousin of the Irish púca and perhaps of Shakespeare's Puck.

cabbyl_ushtey.name: Kelpie (Cabbyl-ushtey)
cabbyl_ushtey.fact: On the Isle of Man the water horse is called the cabbyl-ushtey, and it is the Manx cousin of the Scottish kelpie.

moddey_dhoo.name: Black Shuck (Moddey Dhoo)
moddey_dhoo.fact: The Moddey Dhoo is the black dog said to haunt Peel Castle on the Isle of Man.

orcadian.name: Selkie (Orcadian)
orcadian.fact: Selkie stories are told most strongly in Orkney and Shetland, where the seal-folk were said to shed their skins on the shore.

skomer.name: Volet (Skomer)
skomer.fact: The Skomer vole is a bank vole subspecies found only on Skomer island, and it is larger than the mainland animal.
